newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas soybean plantings running ahead of normal.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas soybean plantings running ahead of normal.

text.p: Soybean plantings in Arkansas were running ahead of normal as of Sunday, according to the state's weekly Agricultural Statistics Service update.
Soybeans were 62 percent planted, up from 52 percent a week earlier and ahead of the five-year average of 55 percent. Emergence reached 49 percent, versus an average of 41 percent.
Condition ratings also improved with 61 percent in the good or excellent categories, up from 56 percent a week ago.
The report noted below normal temperatures and below normal rainfall prevailed across the state.
Soft red winter wheat ratings improved slightly to six percent excellent, 28 percent good, 45 percent fair, 18 percent poor and three percent very poor.
Cotton was 99 percent emerged and three percent squared versus five-year averages of 94 and nine percent.

Rice was 96 percent emerged, up from an average pace for the date of 93 percent. Ratings improved slightly to five percent excellent, 43 percent good, 37 percent fair and five percent poor. "Rice flooding was reported by several districts," the report said.
